worked_solution:
By Newton’s second law,

$$
F(t)=ma(t),
$$

where $F(t)$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a(t)$ is the acceleration.

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\cdot \operatorname{arcsin}⁡(t)+t\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(t)) \\  & =1\cdot \operatorname{arcsin}⁡(t)+t\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(t)+\frac{t}{\sqrt{1-{t}^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F(t) & =ma(t) \\  & =8\cdot (\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(t)+\frac{t}{\sqrt{1-{t}^{2}}}) \\  & =8\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(t)+\frac{8t}{\sqrt{1-{t}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
